records.summary: Score one 32ms window of 16kHz mono audio for human-speech risk using a real Silero VAD model forward pass.
records.description: A single-chunk speech-risk scorer: given exactly 512 samples (32ms) of 16kHz mono PCM plus the model's own carried streaming state (a 64-sample audio context and an LSTM (h,c) pair, all optional -- default to a cold start), runs one real Silero VAD (snakers4/silero-vad, MIT) forward pass -- reflect-pad, an STFT-as-Conv1d front end, a 4-layer Conv1d+ReLU encoder, one LSTMCell step, a final Conv1d, and a sigmoid -- and returns a speech probability plus the updated context/state to carry into the next chunk. It does not chunk a whole recording, apply a decision threshold, merge adjacent windows into segments, or decide anything about export/sharing -- that is a caller-owned policy over a stream of these scores (mirrors how classifier.release-gate-evaluate and classification.outcome-resolve keep policy separate from scoring). It does not resample audio, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow. On malformed input it fails closed: status is invalid_input and speech_probability is 1.0 (maximum caution), never a false all-clear.
scenarios: As an audio operator, I want a quiet or silent window scored with low speech probability, so that a caller's downstream policy can let genuinely quiet audio through.

As an audio operator, I want the model's own streaming context and LSTM state threaded from one window's output into the next window's input, so that scoring a real recording chunk by chunk matches scoring it in one pass.
As an audio operator, I want a window of the wrong length rejected with maximum-caution output rather than silently scored, so that a malformed chunk can never look like verified-safe audio.
As an audio operator, I want a malformed carried-context array rejected even when the new samples are valid, so that a corrupted streaming state can never silently reset to a false all-clear.

records.summary: Transform a bounded interleaved signed-16 PCM chunk deterministically.
records.description: Portable pure signal transformation over supplied PCM samples. Downsampling applies a bounded box-average low-pass before decimation; upsampling uses deterministic linear interpolation. This basic filter is not a studio-grade polyphase resampler and requires acoustic-corpus quality evaluation before recognition-quality claims. It converts one- or two-channel layouts and does not decode containers, read/write artifacts, capture devices, choose models, or know a location or application. Call once per bounded chunk; large recordings must be streamed by the Traverse runtime.
scenarios: As an audio-processing capability consumer, I want PCM resampled and downmixed to a model profile so that inference receives consistent bounded chunks.

As an audio-processing capability consumer, I want unsupported rates, channel layouts, malformed samples, and resource-exceeding outputs rejected so that the module fails deterministically within its memory budget.

records.summary: Transcribe speech to text from 16kHz mono audio using a real Whisper-tiny encoder-decoder transformer forward pass (greedy, English-forced decoding).
records.description: Runs a real openai/whisper-tiny forward pass -- 80-channel log-mel spectrogram front end, a 2-conv1d/4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer encoder, a 4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer decoder with causal self-attention and cross-attention to the full encoder output, then greedy (argmax, no beam search) autoregressive decoding seeded with a fixed startoftranscript/English/transcribe/no-timestamps prompt -- an officially-sanctioned, documented minimal decoding path (HF's own generation_config.json ships this exact forced-token configuration for this model). Not a KV-cached decoder: each step recomputes the full decoder stack over the token sequence so far, which is correctness-first and entirely tractable at this model's scale. Complements audio.detect-speech-segments (registry#460): an app that already gates on 'is there speech in this clip' is a short step from 'what did it say'. Input is up to 30 seconds (480000 samples) of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; shorter clips are zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window (longer audio must be pre-chunked by the caller -- this capability does not chunk or stream). Known, documented limitations: output capped at 224 decoded tokens; English-only (language is forced, not detected -- non-English input transcribes as attempted English); greedy single-hypothesis decoding, so exact wording (e.g. punctuation) can differ slightly from a beam-search reference without being wrong. Does not detect speech presence/absence (see audio.detect-speech-segments for that), translate, diarize speakers, produce timestamps, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.
scenarios: As a meeting organizer, I want spoken audio transcribed to text, so that I can search, summarize, or extract entities from what was said without a separate ASR service.
As a meeting organizer, I want silent or empty audio to come back as an empty transcript rather than a hallucinated guess, so that gaps in a recording don't produce fabricated text.

As a meeting organizer, I want an explicit model_unavailable status rather than a silent empty transcript when the artifact was built without its weight table, so that a misconfigured deployment fails loudly instead of quietly returning nothing.

records.summary: Transcribe speech to text from 16kHz mono audio using a real Whisper-tiny encoder-decoder transformer forward pass, gated on a Silero VAD speech-presence pre-check so it never hallucinates a transcript for non-speech audio.
records.description: Runs a real openai/whisper-tiny forward pass -- 80-channel log-mel spectrogram front end, a 2-conv1d/4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer encoder, a 4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer decoder with causal self-attention and cross-attention to the full encoder output, then greedy (argmax, no beam search) autoregressive decoding seeded with a fixed startoftranscript/English/transcribe/no-timestamps prompt -- an officially-sanctioned, documented minimal decoding path (HF's own generation_config.json ships this exact forced-token configuration for this model). New in 1.1.0: before running the (expensive) encoder/decoder at all, the input is scored by audio.detect-speech-segments' Silero VAD engine (registry#460, reused directly, not duplicated) in its own fixed 512-sample chunks; if no chunk anywhere in the clip clears a speech-probability threshold, the capability returns an empty transcript immediately. This fixes a real, observed failure mode in 1.0.0: Whisper has no notion of 'is this speech at all' and would confidently transcribe non-speech, non-silent audio (a tone, music, noise) as plausible-sounding text -- a synthetic sine wave came back as ' [MUSIC PLAYING]'. True silence was already handled by a cheap energy-threshold check; this closes the gap for non-silent non-speech audio. Not a KV-cached decoder: each step recomputes the full decoder stack over the token sequence so far, which is correctness-first and entirely tractable at this model's scale. Complements audio.detect-speech-segments (registry#460) directly (reuses its engine rather than merely being conceptually related to it): an app that already gates on 'is there speech in this clip' is a short step from 'what did it say', and this capability now performs that same check internally by default. Input is up to 30 seconds (480000 samples) of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; shorter clips are zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window (longer audio must be pre-chunked by the caller -- this capability does not chunk or stream). Known, documented limitations: output capped at 224 decoded tokens; English-only (language is forced, not detected -- non-English input transcribes as attempted English, once past the speech-presence gate); greedy single-hypothesis decoding, so exact wording (e.g. punctuation) can differ slightly from a beam-search reference without being wrong; the speech-presence gate is a presence check (any chunk clearing the threshold proceeds), not a duration/coverage measurement, so a clip that is mostly non-speech with one brief speech burst is still fully transcribed. Does not translate, diarize speakers, produce timestamps, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.
scenarios: As a meeting organizer, I want spoken audio transcribed to text, so that I can search, summarize, or extract entities from what was said without a separate ASR service.
As a meeting organizer, I want silent or empty audio to come back as an empty transcript rather than a hallucinated guess, so that gaps in a recording don't produce fabricated text.

As a meeting organizer, I want a tone, music, or other non-speech-but-not-silent audio to come back as an empty transcript rather than a confident hallucination, so that a recording's non-speech portions don't pollute a transcript with fabricated text.

As a meeting organizer, I want an explicit model_unavailable status rather than a silent empty transcript when the artifact was built without its weight table, so that a misconfigured deployment fails loudly instead of quietly returning nothing.

core.authorize is a pure, side-effect-free authorization capability designed for maximum reusability across web, mobile, desktop, edge, and AI-agent runtimes.

It deliberately separates policy definition from policy evaluation. The caller supplies a complete, versioned policy configuration at invocation time (or a compact reference in future extensions). - Fail-closed by default (default_effect = deny).
- Fully deterministic: identical inputs always produce identical outputs.
- No host, network, or filesystem access.

- Explicit support for multi-tenant isolation, hierarchical roles, time/context conditions, ownership, relationships, high-priority denies, and break-glass overrides.

- The evaluator implements a practical subset of common authorization patterns; it is not a full XACML or Cedar engine.

Configuration defines allowed transitions and whether only the owner may perform them. The capability never mutates external state — callers apply the returned decision.

Council/product alignment note: workflows declare a `snoozed` status for follow-through; this contract includes `snoozed` in the status enum and default transition examples so WF3/WF4 compose without a silent schema gap.

records.summary: Deterministic state machine for action item status transitions (open → in_progress → blocked → snoozed → done / cancelled).
records.description:
Pure state-machine for action-item status transitions under a caller-supplied transition_config (allowed_transitions + owner_only).

Implemented and smoke-tested matrix (use_cases):
- open → in_progress (ok)
- done → open illegal (illegal_transition)
- open → snoozed (ok)
- non-owner denied (not_owner)
- in_progress → blocked (ok)
- in_progress → done (ok)
- blocked → in_progress (ok)
- snoozed → open (ok)
- open → cancelled (ok)
- cancelled → open illegal (covers current_status=cancelled)
- missing current_status → invalid_status

Known limitations (intentional in 1.1.0):
- Transition graph is entirely caller-supplied; no built-in default policy
- Does not persist status changes
scenarios: As an owner, I want to move an item from open to in_progress, so that active work is reflected accurately.
As a system, I want an illegal transition (done → open) rejected, so that completed work cannot silently reopen.
As an owner, I want to snooze an open item, so that I can pause follow-up without losing the item.
As a system, I want a non-owner blocked when owner_only is true, so that only the owner can change status.
As an owner, I want in_progress → blocked, so that blockers are an explicit status, not tribal knowledge.
As an owner, I want in_progress → done, so that finished work can leave the active queue.
As an owner, I want blocked → in_progress, so that cleared blockers resume cleanly.
As an owner, I want snoozed → open, so that snoozed items re-enter the follow-up pool.
As an owner, I want open → cancelled, so that abandoned work can exit without fake completion.
As a system, I want cancelled items to reject further transitions, so that cancelled work stays terminal.
As a system, I want missing current_status rejected with invalid_status, so that incomplete transition requests fail closed.

records.description:
Gatekeeper capability used when turning extracted candidates into real tracked items (Loop WF2). Enforces data quality rules that are configurable per workspace via `validation_config`. Pure and deterministic — never mutates storage.

Checks covered by this guest:
- non-empty title
- optional required owner / due date
- past-due rejection when `allow_past_due` is false
- duplicate detection (`none` | `title` | `title_and_owner`) against `existing_open_items`

records.summary: Validates a single action item for required fields, owner existence, due-date sanity and duplicate detection before it becomes a commitment.
records.description:
Gatekeeper for action-item commitments: title/owner/due-date rules and duplicate detection under validation_config. Pure and deterministic.

Implemented and smoke-tested matrix (use_cases):
- complete item validates (ok)
- past due rejected when allow_past_due=false (validation_failed)
- missing owner when require_owner=true (validation_failed)
- duplicate title+owner (duplicate)
- duplicate title-only check mode (duplicate)
- invalid duplicate_check config (invalid_config)

Known limitations (intentional in 1.1.0):
- Does not verify owner_id exists in a directory; only presence/absence
- Date parsing is YYYY-MM-DD lexical compare only
scenarios: As a meeting organizer confirming extracted items, I want a complete item to validate cleanly, so that good commitments can be committed without friction.
As a system, I want an item with a past due date rejected when allow_past_due is false, so that stale due dates cannot sneak through.
As a system, I want a missing owner rejected when require_owner is true, so that ownerless commitments never enter the board.
As a system, I want a duplicate title+owner against open items rejected, so that the same commitment is not tracked twice.
As a system, I want duplicate_check=title to reject matching titles regardless of owner, so that title-only uniqueness can be enforced.
As a system, I want an unknown duplicate_check value rejected with invalid_config, so that bad validation config fails closed.

IMPORTANT: this artifact is a fixed-output deterministic fixture -- it does not read or process the `document` input at all; every call returns the same hardcoded docType/parties/amounts/confidence/recommendation values regardless of what document is submitted. It is a genuine, real WASI binary (not a placeholder stub sharing a digest with unrelated capabilities), useful for proving the registry/artifact-hosting/execution pipeline end-to-end, but it does not perform real document analysis. Tracked follow-up for real per-input logic: registry#79.

records.summary: Analyze a submitted document into deterministic approval-review fields using simple keyword/heuristic rules.
records.description: Real, deterministic document approval analysis: genuinely reads the `document` input and derives its fields via simple keyword classification (docType), a two-consecutive-capitalized-word heuristic (parties), and a `$`-prefixed number scan (amounts) -- no model, network, randomness, or host state dependency, matching this capability's original design constraints. This replaces the 1.0.1 release, which was a fixed-output fixture that ignored its input entirely. Known limitation, disclosed rather than hidden: the party-extraction heuristic is intentionally simple and can false-positive on any two consecutive capitalized words at a sentence start (e.g. "This Agreement"), not just genuine named parties -- acceptable for a reference-tier, no-model capability, not production-grade named-entity recognition. Source: agents/doc-approval-analyze/ in this repo.

records.summary: Format a numeric amount as a currency display string, with correct decimal places and symbol placement for a disclosed, finite set of currency/locale combinations.
records.description: Formats amount as a currency string using currency_code's standard minor-unit decimal places and locale's symbol-placement convention, both drawn from a small fixed, disclosed table covering exactly 8 currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, INR, BHD) and 5 locales (en-US, en-GB, de-DE, fr-FR, ja-JP) -- not a live ISO 4217 registry and not full ICU/CLDR data; see SPEC.md for the exact table. An unrecognized currency_code or locale falls back to a generic '<CODE> <amount>' format rather than guessing, and supported: false is returned so the caller can detect the fallback rather than silently trusting an unstyled result. Negative amounts are formatted with a leading minus sign before the symbol (e.g. '-$12.50'), not locale-specific parenthetical negative notation, in this version.

records.summary: Extract named entities (person, organization, location, misc) from free text using a real DistilBERT-NER model forward pass.
records.description: Runs a real DistilBERT (dslim/distilbert-NER, Apache-2.0) token-classification forward pass -- WordPiece tokenize (case-preserving; capitalization is real signal for this model), 6 transformer layers, per-token BIO-tag classification, then merge adjacent B-/I- tags of the same type into entity spans with byte offsets into the input text. Returns an array of {text, label, start, end} (label one of PER, ORG, LOC, MISC; start/end are UTF-8 byte offsets). A real model forward pass at execution time, not a keyword list or a 'leading capitalized word' heuristic. Known limitation, faithfully reproduced rather than hidden: this compact model sometimes tags interior WordPieces of a multi-piece entity with a fresh B- tag instead of a continuing I- tag, which this capability's BIO merge (correctly) reports as separate adjacent entities rather than guessing they should be one -- e.g. 'Acme Corp' can come back as three short spans. Does not resolve entities against a knowledge base, deduplicate mentions, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.
scenarios: As a meeting organizer, I want person, organization, and location entities extracted from a sentence, so that a caller can build a structured summary without a keyword list.
As a meeting organizer, I want a well-known person, organization, and location correctly grouped into single clean spans when the model tags them consistently, so that common cases read naturally.
As a meeting organizer, I want text with no named entities to return an empty array rather than a forced guess, so that ordinary sentences aren't mislabeled.
As a meeting organizer, I want empty input to return an empty array rather than an error, so that an empty upstream field never breaks the pipeline.

records.summary: Identify the language of free text using a from-scratch character-trigram frequency classifier trained on 24 languages.
records.description: Normalizes input text (collapse whitespace, lowercase, pad), extracts its own top-400 character trigrams by frequency, and scores each of 24 trained languages by the integer rank-distance between the text's trigrams and that language's top-300 trigram frequency profile (Cavnar & Trenkle 1994, 'N-Gram-Based Text Categorization') -- a trigram absent from a language's profile costs a fixed max penalty. Returns the lowest-distance language, an integer 0-100 confidence derived from the margin to the second-best language, and the top-3 candidate languages with their raw distances. Input with fewer than 5 distinct trigrams (very short or empty text) returns 'und' (undetermined) rather than a low-confidence guess. Trained on UDHR (Universal Declaration of Human Rights) translations across ar, bg, cs, da, de, el, en, es, fi, fr, he, hi, hu, id, it, ja, nl, pl, pt, ro, ru, sv, ta, uk. Not a port of CLD2 or any other existing language-ID library -- CLD2 was investigated and found impractical to port faithfully (see registry#469) -- this is an original implementation of a well-documented public technique. Does not detect languages outside the trained set, does not handle mixed-language text (scores the whole input as one language), and does not read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.
scenarios: As a support-ticket router, I want the language of an incoming ticket identified, so that I can route it to the right glossary/locale before further processing.
As a support-ticket router, I want a clear 'undetermined' result rather than a false guess when there isn't enough text to classify responsibly, so that I don't misroute short or empty input.

records.summary: Truncate free text to a caller-supplied Unicode-scalar length budget, with an optional ellipsis included inside that budget.
records.description: Counts Rust char values (Unicode scalar values), not UTF-8 bytes or grapheme clusters. If text already fits within max_length, returns it unchanged with truncated=false. Otherwise, returns at most max_length Unicode scalars with truncated=true: by default a single Unicode ellipsis (…); when a custom ellipsis is supplied, the ellipsis is included inside the same total budget. If the ellipsis itself is longer than max_length it is clipped to the budget, and max_length=0 returns an empty string. This capability is deterministic, memory-only, and does not interpret HTML, display width, or grapheme clusters.
scenarios: As a note-taking app developer, I want long note text shortened to a fixed preview budget with the default ellipsis included in that budget, so that list rows stay bounded without exceeding the UI limit.
As a note-taking app developer, I want text that already fits the preview budget returned byte-for-byte unchanged, so that short notes are never modified just because the truncation capability ran.

As a note-taking app developer, I want to choose an ASCII ellipsis while keeping it inside the same total length budget, so that clients with a house style can request three dots without overflowing their preview limit.
As a note-taking app developer, I want a zero-length budget to return an empty preview and report that truncation occurred, so that a disabled preview slot has explicit deterministic behavior.

records.summary: Normalize a phone number to E.164 format and check its digit-count plausibility for its country code.
records.description: Strips formatting characters (spaces, dashes, parentheses), determines a calling code (from an explicit leading '+' or from the default_country input), and checks the remaining digit count against a fixed table of plausible national-number lengths for a supported set of country calling codes. Returns the E.164-formatted number when plausible. This is NOT a carrier/HLR lookup and does NOT verify the number is actually assigned, active, or reachable -- it is pure format/plausibility validation, deterministic and offline, using a small disclosed table of supported country codes (see SPEC.md), not the full ITU-T numbering plan database. line_type is always "unknown" in this version since distinguishing mobile/landline/VoIP requires carrier data this capability does not have access to. Known, disclosed limitation: does NOT strip domestic trunk prefixes (e.g. the leading '0' in how a UK or German number is normally written for in-country dialing, such as '020 7946 0958') -- when relying on default_country rather than an explicit '+' prefix, the caller must supply the number already in national-significant-number form (no leading trunk digit), or normalization will report digit_count_implausible for an otherwise-valid domestic-format number.

records.summary: Score a password's structural strength (length, character-class diversity, common weak patterns) without checking it against any breach database.
records.description: Computes a deterministic 0-4 strength score and a human-readable issue list from structural properties only. Exact model: 1 point each for containing a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter, a digit, and a symbol (a structural score of 0-4); +1 bonus if the password is at least twice min_length; -1 each for a 4+ character sequential run (e.g. '1234', 'abcd', either direction) and a 4+ character immediate repeat (e.g. 'aaaa'); if the password is shorter than min_length, the whole score is capped at 1 regardless of character diversity (a short password is weak even if varied); if require_symbol is true and no symbol is present, the score is capped at 3. Every unmet criterion and triggered penalty is reported individually in issues (not merged into combined messages). Deliberately does NOT check the password against a known-breached-password list (e.g. HaveIBeenPwned) -- that requires a live network call, which is not available to any capability under the current ABI whitelist; a caller wanting breach-checking must do that outside the sandbox, separately, ideally without ever passing the plaintext password to a third-party service uncontrolled by the caller. The password value itself is never included in the output.

records.summary: Score a password's structural strength (length, character-class diversity, common weak patterns) without checking it against any breach database.

records.summary: Check whether a numeric string passes the Luhn checksum, as used by credit card numbers and other identifiers.
records.description: Applies the standard Luhn (mod 10) checksum algorithm to a digit string: doubling every second digit from the rightmost, subtracting 9 from any result over 9, summing all digits, and checking the total is a multiple of 10. This is a checksum-format check only -- it does NOT verify the number belongs to a real, active account, is not stolen, or is authorized for any transaction (none of that is possible without a live call to a card network or issuer, which is not available to any capability under the current ABI whitelist). Luhn validity is necessary but nowhere near sufficient for treating a card number as safe to charge. Formatting characters (spaces, dashes) are stripped before checking when strip_formatting is true (the default); the input is never logged, persisted, or included in the output.
